note: Kho bài đọc hiểu. Mỗi bài 5 câu. kind="rightwrong" là bài Đúng/Sai, kind="mcq" là bài chọn đáp án đúng nhất. Một đề rút một bài mỗi loại.

passages.title: The bookshop that lends chairs
passages.body:
There is a small bookshop on my street that has done something odd for years: it lends out chairs. Not books — chairs. If you live nearby and need extra seats for a party, you can borrow up to eight of them for a day.

The owner, Mr Bang, started this by accident. Twelve years ago a neighbour asked to borrow a few chairs for a wedding, and he agreed because he had them stacked in the back room anyway. Word spread. Now there is a notebook by the till where people write their name and the date.

He does not charge anything. When I asked why, he said the shop is quiet most afternoons and the chairs would only sit there. He also admitted, laughing, that people who come back with the chairs usually buy a book while they are in the shop.

Not everything has gone smoothly. Two chairs came back broken last year and were never replaced. Mr Bang shrugged about it. He says he has lost far more money on books nobody wanted than on chairs nobody returned.

passages.title: My mother's second bicycle
passages.body:
My mother learned to ride a bicycle at forty-three. She had wanted to learn as a child, but there were five children in her family and only one bicycle, and it belonged to her brother.

She did not tell anyone she was learning. Every evening for a month she walked to the empty car park behind the market with a bicycle she had bought second-hand, and she practised there until it was dark. My father thought she was visiting a friend.

The first time we saw her ride, she came down our street with both hands on the handlebars and a very straight back, and she did not stop until she reached the gate. My sister clapped. My mother said nothing at all and went inside to make tea.

She still rides that bicycle to the market twice a week, although my brother has offered many times to buy her a new one. She says the old one knows the way.

passages.title: The man who counts birds
passages.body:
Every Sunday at six in the morning, Mr Tho walks the same three kilometres along the canal and writes down every bird he sees. He has done this for nineteen years. The notebooks fill a shelf in his kitchen.

He is not a scientist. He worked in a shoe factory until he retired, and he started counting because his doctor told him to walk more and he found walking without a purpose boring. The counting gave the walk a point.

For the first ten years nobody was interested. Then a university student found his notebooks while writing about the canal, and now a research group in the city asks him for a copy every year. They told him his records are the only ones anyone kept for that stretch of water.

He is careful about what he claims. When people ask whether there are fewer birds now, he says the numbers go up and down and nineteen years is not very long. But he has not seen a kingfisher there since 2019, and he writes that down too, every Sunday, as a blank.

passages.title: The class that meets on a boat
passages.body:
Twice a month, twenty students from a school in Can Tho have their biology lesson on a boat. The school does not own it. It belongs to a fruit seller called Mrs Diem, who takes the class along the river on the two mornings she is not at the market.

The idea came from a teacher, Mr Vinh, who was tired of showing photographs of river plants to children who lived beside a river. He asked three boat owners before Mrs Diem said yes. She refused payment at first, then agreed to take fuel money only.

The lessons are not easy to run. The boat holds twenty and the class has twenty-six, so the students take turns, and a lesson is cancelled whenever the water is high. Parents had to sign forms, and every student wears a life jacket bought by the school.

Mr Vinh says the change he did not expect was in the quietest students. Several who never spoke in the classroom ask questions on the boat. He has no explanation for it, but he has stopped being surprised.

items.prompt: The bookshop lends chairs as well as selling books.
items.explain: ĐÚNG. Bài mở đầu bằng chính việc này: cửa hàng sách cho mượn ghế.

items.prompt: Mr Bang planned the chair service before he opened the shop.
items.explain: SAI. "Mr Bang started this by accident" — mọi chuyện bắt đầu tình cờ từ một người hàng xóm hỏi mượn.

items.prompt: People have to pay a small amount to borrow the chairs.
items.explain: SAI. "He does not charge anything" — ông không lấy tiền.

items.prompt: Borrowers often buy something when they bring the chairs back.
items.explain: ĐÚNG. Ông thừa nhận người trả ghế thường mua một cuốn sách khi ghé cửa hàng.

items.prompt: Mr Bang was very angry about the two broken chairs.
items.explain: SAI. Ông chỉ nhún vai và nói mình mất tiền vì sách ế còn nhiều hơn.

items.prompt: The writer's mother could not ride a bicycle as a child.
items.explain: ĐÚNG. Nhà có năm anh chị em mà chỉ một xe đạp, và xe đó là của anh trai bà.

items.prompt: Her family helped her practise every evening.
items.explain: SAI. Bà giấu cả nhà; bố người viết còn tưởng bà đi thăm bạn.

items.prompt: She bought a bicycle that had already been used.
items.explain: ĐÚNG. Bài ghi rõ đó là chiếc xe bà mua lại ("second-hand").

items.prompt: She spoke proudly to her family after her first ride.
items.explain: SAI. "My mother said nothing at all" — bà không nói gì mà vào nhà pha trà.

items.prompt: She has refused offers of a newer bicycle.
items.explain: ĐÚNG. Anh trai người viết đã đề nghị mua xe mới nhiều lần nhưng bà vẫn dùng xe cũ.

items.prompt: Why did Mr Tho begin counting birds?

options.text: A university asked him to do it.
He wanted a reason to keep walking.
He studied birds before retiring.
A neighbour lent him a notebook.

items.explain: Bác sĩ bảo ông đi bộ nhiều hơn, nhưng đi không mục đích thì chán, nên việc đếm chim khiến buổi đi bộ có ý nghĩa.

items.prompt: What was Mr Tho's job before he retired?

options.text: He was a teacher at a school.
He worked at a shoe factory.
He was a scientist at a lab.
He worked as a boat driver.

items.explain: Bài nói rõ ông làm ở xưởng giày cho tới khi nghỉ hưu, và nhấn mạnh ông không phải nhà khoa học.

items.prompt: How did other people find out about his notebooks?

options.text: A student came across them.
He sent them to a newspaper.
He gave a talk at a college.
A shop displayed them for him.

items.explain: Một sinh viên đại học tìm thấy các cuốn sổ khi viết bài về con kênh.

items.prompt: What do the researchers say about his records?

options.text: They are the only ones for that place.
They contain too many small errors.
They cover a much wider area now.
They should be published as a book.

items.explain: Nhóm nghiên cứu nói đây là ghi chép duy nhất mà ai đó lưu lại cho đoạn kênh này.

items.prompt: How does Mr Tho answer questions about bird numbers?

options.text: He says the numbers are clearly falling.
He avoids the question completely.
He says his data covers a short time.
He says the canal is much cleaner now.

items.explain: Ông thận trọng: số lượng lên xuống thất thường và mười chín năm chưa phải dài. Ông không khẳng định chim đang giảm.

items.prompt: Who owns the boat used for the lessons?

options.text: It belongs to the school itself.
It belongs to a fruit seller.
It belongs to the biology teacher.
It belongs to a group of parents.

items.explain: Thuyền là của bà Diễm, một người bán trái cây; nhà trường không sở hữu thuyền.

items.prompt: Why did Mr Vinh want to teach on the river?

options.text: The classroom was too small for the class.
He was showing pictures of nearby things.
The school asked him to try something new.
He wanted the students to learn to swim.

items.explain: Ông chán cảnh chiếu ảnh cây cối ven sông cho những đứa trẻ vốn sống ngay bên sông.

items.prompt: What did Mrs Diem finally agree to accept?

options.text: Money to cover the fuel only.
A full payment for each lesson.
Free fruit from the school garden.
Nothing at all for her trouble.

items.explain: Ban đầu bà từ chối nhận tiền, sau chỉ đồng ý nhận tiền dầu.

items.prompt: Why do the students take turns?

options.text: The boat cannot hold the whole class.
Only half the class chose biology.
There are not enough life jackets.
The lessons are held very early.

items.explain: Thuyền chở được hai mươi người trong khi lớp có hai mươi sáu, nên phải thay phiên.

items.prompt: What surprised Mr Vinh about the lessons?

options.text: How much the parents helped him.
How quickly the students learned.
How often the trips were cancelled.
How the shyest students behaved.

items.explain: Điều ông không ngờ là mấy học sinh ít nói nhất trên lớp lại chịu đặt câu hỏi khi ở trên thuyền.
